chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn Abdillah both narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Fudayl al-A'war, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who said:

I met him after the people had prayed 'Asr. He said, 'I have not prayed Dhuhr yet, so do not keep me, and proceed with success.' I asked, 'Why have you delayed it until now?' He said, 'I had a need in the market, so I delayed the prayer until I could pray in the mosque, for the merit that has reached me about it.' I asked, 'What has been narrated about it?' He said, 'So-and-so informed me from so-and-from A'ishah, who said, 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) say: I was ascended to the heavens, and I descended to the earth, then I was brought down to the mosque of my father Nuh (a.s.) and my father Ibrahim, which is the Mosque of Kufa, and I prayed two Rak'ah in it.' Then it was said: The Messenger of Allah (s.a.a.w.) said, 'Verily, the obligatory prayer in it equals a purified Hajj, and the voluntary prayer in it equals a purified 'Umrah.'

key_terms.عُرِجَ بِي: I was ascended (referring to the Prophet's Night Journey)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying in the Mosque of Kufa according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the specific virtue of the Mosque of Kufa, linking it to the Prophet’s Night Journey (Isra) and the intercession of Prophets Noah and Abraham. It establishes a tangible spiritual economy where the reward for obligatory prayers here equals a *Hajj Mabrur* and voluntary prayers equal an *Umrah Mabrur*, a concept deeply cherished in Shia devotional practice for emphasizing the sanctity of key shrines.
